text: How many moles are in \(4.00\ \mathrm{g}\) of sodium hydroxide, \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)? (\(M_r = 40.0\))
What is the relative formula mass of calcium carbonate, \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\)? (\(A_r\): Ca 40.1, C 12.0, O 16.0)
What volume does \(0.250\ \mathrm{mol}\) of a gas take up at room temperature and pressure? (1 mol = \(24.0\ \mathrm{dm^3}\))
\(0.0500\ \mathrm{mol}\) of a solute is dissolved to make \(250\ \mathrm{cm^3}\) of solution. What is the concentration?
Propane burns completely: \(\mathrm{C_3H_8} + x\,\mathrm{O_2 \rightarrow 3CO_2 + 4H_2O}\). What is \(x\)?
working: Oxygen atoms on the right: \(3(2) + 4(1) = 10\), so \(5\ \mathrm{O_2}\)

text: A compound is 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. What is its empirical formula?
\(10.0\ \mathrm{g}\) of \(\mathrm{CaCO_3}\) (\(M_r = 100\)) is heated: \(\mathrm{CaCO_3 \rightarrow CaO + CO_2}\). What mass of \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) is made?
\(25.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}\) of \(\mathrm{NaOH}\) is neutralised by \(20.0\ \mathrm{cm^3}\) of \(0.100\ \mathrm{mol\ dm^{-3}}\) \(\mathrm{HCl}\). What is the concentration of the \(\mathrm{NaOH}\)?
How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in the ion \(^{37}\mathrm{Cl^-}\)? (Cl has \(Z = 17\))
working: Protons \(= Z = 17\), neutrons \(= 37 - 17 = 20\), and the \(-\) charge adds one electron: \(18\)

text: What is the electron configuration of an iron atom, \(\mathrm{Fe}\) (\(Z = 26\))?
working: 18 electrons fill to \(3p^6\); the last 8 go \(4s^2\) then \(3d^6\)

text: What are the shape and bond angle of ammonia, \(\mathrm{NH_3}\)?
working: 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair. The lone pair repels more, squeezing the angle from \(109.5^\circ\) to about \(107^\circ\)

text: Why does water, \(\mathrm{H_2O}\), boil at a much higher temperature than hydrogen sulfide, \(\mathrm{H_2S}\)?

options.text: The O–H covalent bond is stronger than S–H
Water has stronger London forces because it has more electrons
Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other

working: Boiling separates molecules, it does not break covalent bonds. O is small and very electronegative, so water forms hydrogen bonds; \(\mathrm{H_2S}\) does not

text: Which of these elements has the highest first ionisation energy?
working: Across a period nuclear charge rises while shielding barely changes, so the noble gas at the end is highest

text: Why is the first ionisation energy of aluminium lower than that of magnesium?

options.text: Al loses a 3p electron, which is higher in energy and shielded by the 3s electrons
Al has fewer protons than Mg
The 3p electrons in Al are spin-paired and repel each other
Al loses a 3s electron, which is further from the nucleus

working: Mg loses a 3s electron. Al's outer electron is alone in 3p, higher in energy and partly shielded by 3s, so it is easier to remove

text: Which of these molecules is polar?
working: \(\mathrm{H_2O}\) is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel. The other three are symmetrical, so their dipoles cancel

text: What is the H–C–H bond angle in methane, \(\mathrm{CH_4}\)?
working: 4 bonding pairs and no lone pairs repel equally: tetrahedral, \(109.5^\circ\)
